verdict.rationale: mise documents a first-party migration path from asdf: it reads existing `.tool-versions` files as-is, can still use asdf plugins, and reads idiomatic version files such as `.node-version` and `.ruby-version`. Community users confirm it works as a drop-in asdf replacement. This is direct compatibility rather than import or conversion tooling, since no command that converts incumbent configs into `mise.toml` is evidenced. Missing for 10: a documented import/convert command, migration guides for incumbents beyond asdf (e.g. nvm, pyenv, Makefiles), and step-by-step migration documentation.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can migrate an existing project from the incumbent tool with documented import or conversion tooling

citations.quote: Coming from asdf? mise reads `.tool-versions` as-is.
mise is compatible with asdf `.tool-versions` files and can still use asdf plugins when needed.
mise is also compatible with asdf `.tool-versions` files and with idiomatic version files like `.node-version` and `.ruby-version`.
Just using mise as a drop-in asdf replacement has been delightful.
